rationale: Use a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Double the gradient duration while holding composition and temperature fixed to reveal which crowded pairs respond to gradient slope. The initial retention window suggests this should still keep the last peak near or below 10 minutes.

The shallower gradient resolves all but one pair, so test a substantial temperature shift at the same slope to change selectivity. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving headroom under the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Back off temperature by one step to separate the new critical pair while retaining most of the selectivity improvement over 40 C. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, so full resolution would achieve the maximum CRF.

Return to the best temperature and shorten the gradient by one step to test whether the remaining critical pair separates with increased slope. This also reduces retention time; monitor the marginally resolved earlier pair for any loss of resolution.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving the best run’s slope of 0.05 organic fraction per minute. This tests whether a modest starting-composition change can lift the barely unresolved pair above 1.5 without sacrificing the other close pairs, while shortening retention.

At the new starting composition, make the slope modestly shallower to improve the two early critical pairs while using the late pair’s added resolution margin. The final organic fraction remains comfortably above the observed elution window, and the last peak should stay below 10 minutes.

Reduce the slope slightly from 0.04583 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute to bring the marginal early pairs above 1.5 while retaining sufficient late-pair resolution. The endpoint remains above the last peak’s estimated elution composition, with ample time margin below 10 minutes.

Injection 8 already achieves the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark while seeking a shorter fully resolved method. Raise the starting organic fraction and narrow the window, using a shallower slope to compensate for the early pairs’ sensitivity to increased starting strength.

Keep the compact gradient and test a temperature-driven selectivity change, since adjusting slope alone may improve one critical pair while worsening another. Injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark; this run explores an alternative route to full resolution.

Test the compact gradient at 40 C to move beyond the close-pair crossings seen at 50 C and explore a different selectivity regime. All peaks should remain observable and likely below 10 minutes; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.
Lower temperature one step to move the nearly co-eluting pair at 40 C away from its selectivity crossing. The other pairs have resolution margin, and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes.

Test the lower temperature limit to move beyond the remaining early-pair crossing and the late-pair convergence at 35 C. This explores a distinct selectivity window while retaining injection 8 as the proven maximum-score method.

Shorten the newly fully resolved 25 C method by one gradient-duration step to test its resolution margin and reduce the last-peak time. Keep both maximum-score methods as benchmarks if the steeper gradient compromises a critical pair.

Test a substantially steeper gradient to see whether the slope-sensitive critical pair separates again after an elution-order crossover. The higher endpoint should also accelerate the hold-eluting late peaks; injection 8 remains the proven maximum-score benchmark.

Refine the fast 25 C regime with a slightly shallower slope to improve the compressed middle and late pairs. Lower the starting organic fraction simultaneously to shift selectivity within the middle cluster, targeting full resolution well below 7.45 minutes.

Test a 5 C increase on the fastest promising method to adjust its three marginal pairs without lengthening the gradient. This isolates temperature selectivity in the steep-gradient regime while retaining injection 8 as the maximum-score benchmark.

Shift the fully resolved injection 13 gradient upward by 0.05 while preserving its slope to shorten retention and keep late peaks inside the gradient. This tests whether its resolution margin can support a faster low-temperature method; injection 8 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Raise temperature one step to test whether selectivity rescues the sole unresolved pair in injection 18 while shortening retention. The other pairs have resolution margin, making this a targeted refinement of the compact low-temperature method.

Raise the starting composition to shorten retention and shift the early cluster, while making the gradient shallower to recover resolution in its slope-sensitive pair. This targets the opposing deficiencies in injection 19; injection 8 remains the proven maximum-score method.

Make the gradient shallower at fixed starting composition and temperature to improve injection 20’s sole unresolved pair. The other pairs have some resolution margin, and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes, offering another route to the maximum CRF.

Return to injection 18’s selectivity and modestly reduce the slope from 0.0375 to 0.0333 to improve its sole unresolved pair. The higher endpoint keeps late peaks within the gradient, and the estimated last-peak time remains below 10 minutes.

Raise the starting organic fraction to shorten the fully resolved low-temperature method, compensating with a shallower slope to protect its critical pair. Injection 8 remains the fastest proven maximum-score method; this tests whether the alternative selectivity window can approach it.

Reduce the slope from 0.0286 to 0.025 at fixed starting composition and temperature to lift injection 23’s sole unresolved pair. Its late pairs have resolution margin, and the last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially restoring the maximum CRF.

Use the final injection to test whether a temperature shift moves the late pair beyond its convergence near 30 C while retaining resolution in the early cluster and shortening retention. Injection 8 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method and already achieves the maximum CRF of 1.000.
